inputs.text: Local organizers in southern Alberta are gathering signatures for the Water Not Coal petition that Corb Lund launched last month. This citizen initiative is calling on the Government of Alberta to “prohibit through legislation all coal exploration.” From where I stand, this kind of grassroots pushback is essential for taking on the systemic power of extractive industries that always put corporate profits ahead of communities and the shared resources we all rely on. It lays bare the structural failures in our institutions, with their long history of exploitation that keeps threatening the water and land people depend on—hitting the most vulnerable groups hardest through environmental harm and deepening inequality. Real change comes when ordinary people organize like this to demand public welfare over destructive development that serves only the powerful.
